title: Teach the write guard's parser to see past the first command and through shell wrappers
action: Two confirmed P1 bypasses, both in how the token list is built and consumed -- fix them at the shared helpers so every consumer inherits the fix, never at one door. (1) paths.rs find_git_invocation returns at the FIRST token whose basename is git and never scans later separator-delimited segments, so `git status && git stash` is allowed while `git stash` is refused. Turn it into find_git_invocations returning EVERY invocation in the token list; update its one caller in checks.rs (~line 599) to loop, first refusing invocation wins. (2) guards.rs tokenize folds a quoted span into one token and nothing knows sh/bash/eval execute their argument, so `sh -c 'echo x > .bee/state.json'` and `eval 'git stash'` are allowed while the bare forms are refused. Add tokenize_deep: tokenize, then expand wrapper payloads in place and re-scan. A wrapper is a token whose BASENAME equals sh, bash, dash, zsh or ksh followed by -c and a payload token, or the token eval followed by its arguments up to the next separator. Splice the payload's tokens in fenced by `;` so a wrapper can never join two segments. Bound recursion at depth 4. Route the three write-guard consumers through tokenize_deep: guards.rs (~304, bash target extraction), detectors.rs (~226), checks.rs (~598). Leave cli_shape.rs on the plain tokenize -- it parses bee's own argv shape, where a wrapper is not a thing.

truths: A denied command stays denied when any allowed command is placed before it, after any of && || ; |
A denied command stays denied when wrapped in sh -c, bash -c or eval, including a state-file redirect and a git verb
The guard still fails open on an undecidable payload -- this cell must not turn an unparseable command into a silent allow
artifacts: Tests for: compound git after each of && || ; | ; sh -c / bash -c / eval wrapping both a git verb and a .bee/state.json redirect; a nested wrapper; the depth-4 bound

Negative controls proving no over-blocking: `echo "git stash"` and `git commit -m "wip && git stash"` stay allowed, `git -C sub status` and `git --git-dir=.git log` still parse as today, and a path whose basename merely contains sh (scripts/shell/thing.sh) is not treated as a wrapper
prohibitions: Do not fix this in checks.rs alone -- target extraction and the secret-path deny must inherit it too
Do not weaken or delete any existing guard test to make the new behaviour fit

verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml, plus a live probe with the freshly built binary: `git status && git stash` must now refuse, `sh -c 'echo x > .bee/state.json'` must now refuse, and `echo "git stash"` must still pass.
